Effective clinical FTE of a sex-stratified headcount cohort

Source: R/urps_fte_sex.R
urps_effective_fte_sex.Rd

Sex-aware counterpart to urps_effective_fte(): computes scale * sum(n * urps_fte_weight_sex(age, sex, pathway, ...)) for a cohort data.frame that carries per-row sex. Use urps_fte_scale_sex() to anchor the reference cohort's FTE to its headcount before comparing across years or geographies.

Usage

urps_effective_fte_sex(
  counts,
  scale = 1,
  late_from_age = NULL,
  late_factor = 1
)

Arguments

counts

A data.frame with columns age, sex, pathway, and n. Mixed-sex rows are handled natively (no pre-splitting required).

scale

Normalization scale from urps_fte_scale_sex() (default 1 = raw hours/40 weighted sum).

late_from_age, late_factor

Passed to urps_fte_weight_sex().

Value

A length-1 numeric (clinical FTE in 40-hrs/wk units after scaling).

See also

urps_fte_scale_sex(), urps_fte_weight_sex(), urps_effective_fte()

Other URPS FTE sex: URPS_FTE_REFERENCE_HOURS_PER_WEEK, URPS_FTE_SEX_HOURS_VERSION, urps_fte_predicted_hours(), urps_fte_scale_sex(), urps_fte_sex_hours_params(), urps_fte_weight_sex(), urps_supply_fte_sex()

Examples

cs <- data.frame(
  age     = c(45L, 62L, 45L, 62L),
  sex     = c("female", "female", "male", "male"),
  pathway = c("ABOG", "ABOG", "ABU", "ABU"),
  n       = c(350, 150, 100, 40)
)
urps_effective_fte_sex(cs, scale = urps_fte_scale_sex(cs))
#> [1] 640
